text:
Kaiden Guhle plays big minutes for Montreal, 22.7 a night, and the coverage around him lately is about leadership. Yardbarker ran "Kaiden Guhle Becoming A Leader On The Canadiens Blueline," and The Athletic's Arpon Basu wrote on how the Canadiens change when Mike Matheson plays with him.

The numbers are harder on him. At five on five, Montreal has held only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Guhle on the ice, more than ten points worse than when he sits. What has covered it is luck in his favour: the goals with him on the ice have run about 8 better than the chances deserved. That is goaltending and finishing doing him a favour, and it rarely lasts all season.

The tools are real. His top speed, 22.7 mph, sits in the 95th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%.

With 6 points in 17 games he's on pace with his range. The thing to watch is whether the shot share climbs before the bounces stop covering it.
